steps.name: Sample structure QC
caveats: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

plan.title: Hallmark signature scores: Crohn ileum vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is a per-sample, per-signature readout: score all 50 MSigDB hallmark sets in each of the 12 ileum samples (6 Crohn inflamed, 6 control) and test which signatures differ between conditions. The data are gene-level Salmon counts (12,000 genes x 13 columns incl. IDs), one batch, unpaired, with sample_01 at ~4x below median library size. Rank-based UCell scoring is the method of record because ranks within a sample do not depend on library depth, which directly addresses the shallow sample; scores are then tested with limma under the condition design with BH correction across the 50 signatures. The shallow sample is kept (count models down-weight it via size factors; rank-based scores are depth-robust) but inspected in QC and re-tested in a leave-one-out sensitivity step so every significant signature is reported with and without it. Hallmark gene sets are staged at MSigDB 2026.1 human symbols GMT; provenance (version, genes present per set) is recorded per rule R-0134.
